newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police break up Mafia clan, arrest 22.
newsitem.headline: Italian police break up Mafia clan, arrest 22.

text.p: Italian police said on Saturday they had dealt a blow to a gang allied with jailed Mafia boss Benedetto "Nitto" Santapaola by arresting 22 alleged mobsters.

Police said they seized the suspects in dawn raids near the western Sicilian towns of Acireale and Giarre, near Catania. Ten others already in prison were notified they were being investigated in the case.
The suspects faced charges of murder, theft, extortion and illegal possession of arms, police said.
Their clan was believed to be close to Santapaola, who is accused of some of the most violent Mafia attacks in recent years.

He is one of 24 people, including bosses Salvatore Riina, Leoluca Bagarella and Giovanni Brusca, who went on trial last month for a string of bombings in Rome, Florence and Milan that killed 10 people in 1993.
Santapaola is also suspected of involvement in the car bomb murder of magistrate Paolo Borsellino and five bodyguards in Palermo in July 1992.
